original_statement: Domain-separated hash-input records: every hash on the signing path is a typed, domain-separated hash-input record — never ad-hoc concatenation
restatement: Every hash the module computes on the signing path must go through a typed, domain-separated hash-input record, never raw concatenated bytes: (s1) every hash call site takes such a record as input, never ad-hoc concatenation; (s2) hashing the same underlying content bytes under two different domains always produces different digests — domain separation is load-bearing, not decorative.

restatement_clauses.text: Every hash call site on the signing path takes a typed, domain-separated hash-input record as input — never raw concatenated bytes.
Hashing the same underlying content bytes under two different domains (record types/contexts) always produces different digests.

goal: A committed, typed hash-input record wrapper in the module core, used at every hash call site on the signing path, so hashing domain-separates by construction — verified by a test demonstrating two different domains hashing identical underlying content yield different digests (mirroring FS-3).
acceptance_criteria: Every hash call site on the signing path takes a typed, domain-separated hash-input record as input — never raw concatenated bytes.
Hashing the same underlying content bytes under two different domains (record types/contexts) always produces different digests.

request_clauses.text: Every hash call site on the signing path takes a typed, domain-separated hash-input record as input — never raw concatenated bytes.
Hashing the same underlying content bytes under two different domains (record types/contexts) always produces different digests.

acceptance_tests.proves: Across the explored space of hash-input record shapes and domain tags, the real encoding matches an independently-implemented reference encoder for the same domain-separated record scheme at every reachable state — proving hashing goes through the structured record type as specified, not an ad-hoc concatenation that happens to look similar for one sampled input.
acceptance_tests.description: Every hash call site on the signing path takes a typed, domain-separated hash-input record as input — never raw concatenated bytes.

acceptance_tests.proves: Hashing identical underlying content under two or more distinct domains never produces a colliding digest across sampled trials — domain separation actually changes the hash, not just the record's cosmetic shape.
acceptance_tests.description: Hashing the same underlying content bytes under two different domains (record types/contexts) always produces different digests.
